thesis: Dell printed a new 52-week high today and the +20.9% 60-day move has two identifiable drivers this run could not rank against each other. Company-specific: Volta, an Nvidia-backed AI infrastructure startup, emerged from stealth on Aug 4 with a $10B AI-lab partnership and named Dell as the technology provider for its first AI factory, a 133MW Vera Rubin deployment in Norway using PowerEdge XE9812 servers. Sector-wide: reporting attributes today's leg to AI-server demand guidance from Super Micro lifting the whole hardware group, plus a Goldman Sachs Buy reaffirmation and a raised $510 target, which is analyst opinion rather than disclosure. The company-disclosed backdrop is fiscal Q1 (May 28), reported as AI-optimized server revenue of $16.1B, a $51.3B backlog and full-year revenue guidance raised toward $167B with roughly $60B of AI server revenue expected. Dell's fiscal Q2 report is due in the second half of August; no source read this run confirmed the date, so it is treated as an unresolved catalyst rather than a scheduled one.
invalidation: Fiscal Q2 showing AI-server backlog conversion or margins below the raised full-year guidance, or the Volta deployment being rescoped or reassigned.

thesis: Corcept's Q2 calendar-2026 results are a confirmed company disclosure: revenue of $256.1M, up 32% year over year, alongside a raised 2026 revenue outlook of $950M-$1.05B, which the company frames as more than 30% growth. Relacorilant's FDA approval in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer is already granted rather than pending (PDUFA date July 11, 2026). The +33% 60-day move is consistent with those disclosures plus a reported analyst upgrade. The counter-case that the price already discounts the story - the stock is up about 132% year to date and one screen scores its value poorly - is partly answerable: the raise is a company disclosure of a higher revenue base, not multiple expansion alone. What this run cannot settle is the second indication: the FDA issued a complete response letter for relacorilant in Cushing's syndrome on Dec 31, 2025, Corcept resubmitted on June 17, 2026 and expects a six-month review, pointing to a decision around mid-December 2026 - outside the ~90-day risk_flags window but a live binary this run cannot handicap.
invalidation: 2026 revenue tracking below the $950M low end of company guidance, or a second complete response letter on the Cushing's syndrome resubmission.

thesis: Microsoft's fiscal Q4, reported July 29, is a specific, already-confirmed, company-disclosed catalyst: revenue of $90.01B, up 18% year over year and above the $87.62B consensus; non-GAAP EPS of $4.74 against a $4.24 consensus; Azure up 43% in the quarter versus roughly 40% expected; and FY26 Azure revenue crossing $100B for the first time, up 41%. Management guided fiscal Q1 Azure growth of 45% in constant currency against a 41.4% StreetAccount consensus. The +24.3% 60-day move is accounted for by the post-print re-rating, so the tape and the disclosed facts agree rather than conflict. The strongest counter-case is the standard one on this name - that AI capital spending outruns the cloud revenue funding it - and it is answered concretely rather than merely listed: the CFO stated on the call that the calendar-2026 capex forecast is unchanged, removing the escalation the bear case depends on, and the after-hours gain extended specifically on that comment. Separately, a securities class action alleging misleading statements about the AI and Azure business is pending; its lead-plaintiff deadline of Aug 11, 2026 has already passed and no source read this run shows a scheduled ruling, hearing or trial date, so it is unadjudicated background rather than a dated risk.
invalidation: Azure growth decelerating below the guided 45% constant-currency figure in the fiscal Q1 report, or management revising the calendar-2026 capital expenditure forecast upward.
sources: Bernstein Litowitz Berger & Grossmann (securities class action): https://www.blbglaw.com/cases-investigations/microsoft-corporation

thesis: Coherent reported fiscal Q4 today. Sources read this run describe results that cleared expectations, with datacenter and communications revenue up 59% year over year, fiscal Q1 revenue guided to as much as $2.4B - above the quarter just reported - and co-packaged optics shipping in the second half of 2026. No source read this run stated the headline EPS or total revenue figures, so the print is reported only as described and is not quantified here. Against that, the 60-day decline of 20.9% and today's 2.52x volume day are explained as positioning rather than disclosure: an 11.6% fall on Aug 10 was attributed to an optics-versus-memory rotation argument, and today's drop is described as a sell-the-news move after a run of roughly 105% year to date. This is a sentiment-driven drawdown set against improving disclosed fundamentals, and the run cannot settle which governs from here.
invalidation: Fiscal Q1 datacenter and communications revenue coming in below the guided $2.4B level, or co-packaged optics slipping out of the second half of 2026.

thesis: Astera Labs' Q2, reported Aug 4, is a confirmed company disclosure and a clear beat: record revenue of $392.4M, up 104% year over year and 27% sequentially against roughly $361M expected; non-GAAP EPS of $0.80, beating consensus by $0.11; and Q3 revenue guided to $540-560M, a midpoint implying about 40% sequential growth on the Scorpio X-Series ramp, continued Aries PCIe 6 retimer strength and preproduction Taurus shipments. The stock nonetheless fell 12% on the print and is down 17.1% over the 60-day window. Reporting attributes that to profit-taking after a large prior run and to higher operating expenses from continued roadmap investment - positioning and cost mix rather than a disclosed demand problem. That explanation discounts the fundamental significance of the decline without resolving it, so the read is not net-clear.
invalidation: Q3 revenue landing below the guided $540M floor, or operating expense growth continuing to outpace the guided sequential revenue ramp.

thesis: AMD's Q2, reported Aug 4, is company-disclosed and points both ways, so both halves are quoted. Revenue of $11.54B was up 50% year over year with Data Center revenue of $6.7B up 107% on EPYC and Instinct demand, and sources describe a beat on revenue, profit and guidance. Against that, gross margin of 54% came in below a 56% consensus on near-term Helios AI-infrastructure ramp costs, Client and Gaming were described as weak, and the largest AI catalysts - Helios rack-scale systems and MI450 - are weighted to late Q4 and 2027. The stock fell roughly 6% in the session and 8-9% after hours, and is down 11.7% over the 60-day window. The revenue trajectory argues one way and the margin and timing argue the other; this run cannot establish which dominates.
invalidation: Gross margin failing to recover from the 54% Q2 level in the Q3 report, or a further slip in the Helios and MI450 ramp timing.

thesis: SanDisk's fiscal Q4, reported Aug 5, pairs a large beat with a guide below consensus, and both are company-disclosed. Reported: EPS of $39.25 against $33.28 expected and revenue of $8.97B, up 371.6% year over year. Guided: fiscal Q1 revenue of $10.3-10.8B against a $11.16B consensus. The stock fell as much as 11% on the print, is down 27.5% over the 60-day window and roughly 47% from its June 25 high, while still up about 353% year to date. In a memory name the whole debate is how long the cycle runs, and a first guide below consensus is the disclosed data point that debate turns on. A counter-case exists and was engaged - multi-year volume-and-price commitments on datacenter revenue, BiCS8 reaching the majority of bit production exiting FY2026, fabs at full utilisation - but this run cannot settle it against the guidance, so the evidence stays offsetting.
invalidation: Fiscal Q1 revenue printing at or above the $11.16B consensus, or NAND contract pricing holding through the quarter.

thesis: Rocket Lab's Q2 is company-disclosed and points both ways. Record quarterly revenue of $234.07M, up 62% year over year, and a backlog of $2.36B on one side; a loss of $0.08 per share against $0.05 expected on the other. The decisive item is schedule: management said the window for an end-of-year Neutron launch is narrowing and the debut could move into 2027, while still targeting delivery to the pad in Q4 2026, and reporting attributes the post-print fall - shares down roughly 9.6% premarket and about 4% at the open - to that timeline rather than to the revenue line. Liquidity was boosted by a $1.08B equity raise disclosed alongside the quarter. With the single largest value driver's date now uncertain, this run cannot reach a net read, and the 26.7% 60-day decline is consistent with the schedule risk rather than with the revenue print.
invalidation: Neutron confirmed on the pad with a firm Q4 2026 launch date, or the debut slipping past the first half of 2027.

thesis: SpaceX's first report as a public company, on Aug 4, beat on the top line and widened the spending question, and both sides are disclosed. Revenue of $7.8B was up 92% year over year against a $6.8B consensus. The company lost $541M in the quarter following a $4.3B loss in Q1, and first-half capital expenditure reached $28.5B, more than four times the year-ago level, with reporting attributing the roughly 8% after-hours fall specifically to spending on the unprofitable AI segment. The stock is down about 30% from its $150 market debut and roughly 50% from a $225.64 high; this run's own window shows -26.6% over 60 days. A revenue beat and an unresolved cash-burn trajectory point in opposite directions and this run cannot rank them.
invalidation: Capital expenditure decelerating in Q3 while revenue growth holds near the 90% rate, or a third consecutive quarter of widening losses.

thesis: AST SpaceMobile's Q2 business update on Aug 10 missed on both disclosed lines: revenue of $31.5M against a $35.18M consensus and an adjusted loss of $0.77 per share against $0.26 expected, with adjusted operating expenses rising to $119.1M from $91.2M in Q1 and capital expenditure surging to $610.4M from $256.8M. Offsetting that, the company reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $150-200M and completed orbital insertion of BlueBird satellites 11, 12 and 13 in early August. The 18.3% 60-day decline is consistent with the financial miss. The operational milestone and the miss are both company-disclosed and this run cannot resolve which governs, so the evidence is offsetting rather than net-negative or net-positive.
invalidation: Second-half revenue tracking into the reaffirmed $150-200M full-year range, or that guidance being cut.

thesis: Cerebras qualified on volume, not price: 3.16x its 30-bar average on a day the stock fell 11.9% from Wednesday's close, with the 60-day price move only +5.9%. The Q2 print is mixed on the company's own numbers and both halves belong in the record: revenue of $180M missed a $194M estimate, while the loss of $0.05 per share was narrower than expected and full-year guidance was raised. Shares were down 15.9% premarket. Analysts are reported as split, with some reading the sell-off as an entry on cloud revenue growth and improving margins. A topline miss and a guidance raise in the same report is unresolved evidence rather than a net read, and the miss is the item the tape reacted to.
invalidation: Q3 revenue reaching the run-rate implied by the raised full-year guidance, or a second consecutive quarterly revenue miss.

thesis: Corning's Q2, reported July 28, beat and then guided down, both company-disclosed. Adjusted EPS of $0.78 against $0.75 expected on revenue of $4.74B against $4.62B, with Optical Communications up 32% to $2.07B on AI data-center demand; the current-quarter revenue forecast came in below Wall Street consensus, and the CEO cited a shift to long-term customer contracts for optical capacity, heavy capital spending and mixed end markets as near-term execution risks. The stock fell about 12% on the print, posted its worst month in 24 years in July at roughly -46%, and is down 15.6% over this run's 60-day window. The AI-optical demand line and the guide-down pull in opposite directions and this run cannot settle which dominates.
invalidation: Q3 revenue landing at or above consensus, or Optical Communications growth decelerating materially from the 32% rate.

thesis: Micron's 12.7% 60-day decline has no fresh company disclosure behind it that this run could find. Reporting attributes the move to memory-sector demand and pricing concerns - including a company statement that price increases will slow significantly through the quarter - together with a Goldman Sachs downgrade of SK Hynix to Neutral citing expected HBM pricing weakness, and concerns about China capacity additions outpacing DRAM price growth. The stock is down roughly 32% from a June 25 closing high of $1,213.56. That is predominantly a sector-wide and analyst-driven move rather than a company-specific, already-confirmed catalyst, which is not a basis for opening a position in either direction; the trailing revenue base near $37.4B is cited as intact but is not itself news this run verified as new.
invalidation: A company disclosure - quarterly results or formal guidance - that either confirms or contradicts the slowing price-increase read.
